check: whether the remaining goal rounds cover the remaining wall-clock time
why: Earlier this session I checked this and found comfortable headroom. That check used a cadence estimate, and the profile is long enough that a small per-round difference compounds. Re-measured against two anchors rather than an estimate.

measuredCadence.note: Measured between two real observations rather than inferred, because the previous check used an estimate that turned out slightly optimistic.

theProblem.consequence: The profile alone consumes every remaining round, leaving nothing for the GameTest run, Test-S5Release and the closing summary - which need about 5.95 hours of wall clock.

theMitigationThatMakesItFit.insight: The post-profile work does not have to consume a round per six and a half minutes, because the background job mechanism lets a long task span rounds.
theMitigationThatMakesItFit.shape: Start runGameTest as a background job and return; collect it in a later round and start Test-S5Release as another background job; collect and close in a third.
theMitigationThatMakesItFit.revisedTotal: 169 during the profile plus about 10 after is 179 against 169 available

whatThisMeans: The objective is still reachable, but with about an hour less slack than the earlier estimate suggested. The practical consequences are to avoid rounds that do no work, and to start the post-profile tasks as background jobs the moment the profile ends rather than waiting a round to begin.
